cards.explanation: The answer is False. Moses asks, “Please let me return to my brothers in Egypt…” and Jethro, his father-in-law, replies, “Go in peace…” (Exodus 4:18) No stalling and no “stay a little longer.” Some people take twenty minutes to say goodbye at the door, but Jethro keeps it short, friends.

The reason is that the men who wanted to kill Moses are dead. The LORD tells Moses, “Go back to Egypt, for all the men who sought to kill you are dead.” (Exodus 4:19) The ones who wanted him gone are gone themselves. So Moses puts his wife and sons on a donkey and heads for Egypt (Exodus 4:20). He takes the staff of God in his hand, too.
The answer is staff, bakers. “And he took the staff of God in his hand.” (Exodus 4:20) Moses leaves with a family, a donkey and that staff. Everything else is just luggage.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “…I will harden his heart so that he will not let the people go.” (Exodus 4:21) Moses is told to perform the wonders before Pharaoh, and the LORD tells him Pharaoh still won't let the people go. So no quick yes is coming, friends, and Moses hears that before he even gets there.

The answer is “My firstborn son,” friends. The LORD says, “Israel is My firstborn son…” (Exodus 4:22) He doesn't call Israel a project or a crowd. He calls Israel His son. That's the message Moses carries to Pharaoh.

The answer is that the LORD will kill Pharaoh's firstborn son, and it's a heavy one, friends. The LORD tells Moses to say, “…since you have refused to let him go, behold, I will kill your firstborn son!” (Exodus 4:23) I think this is a hard line to read. The LORD says it plainly, and Moses is told to deliver it.

The answer is Zipporah, Moses' wife. She takes a flint knife, cuts off her son's foreskin and touches it to Moses' feet (Exodus 4:25). Then the text says, “So the LORD let him alone.” (Exodus 4:26) I think this is a heavy moment, friends.
The answer is True, bakers. The text says, “So the LORD let him alone.” (Exodus 4:26) It comes right after Zipporah acts. The text doesn't explain more than that, so I'll leave it there too.

The answer is at the mountain of God, friends. Aaron “…met Moses at the mountain of God and kissed him.” (Exodus 4:27) The LORD only said “the wilderness,” and Aaron still found him. Honestly, that's better navigating than I do with a map.

The answer is False. Moses “…told Aaron everything the LORD had sent him to say, and all the signs He had commanded him to perform.” (Exodus 4:28) He doesn't hold anything back, bakers. Aaron is fully in the loop, which makes this the opposite of a surprise party.

The answer is Aaron, friends. “…Aaron relayed everything the LORD had said to Moses.” (Exodus 4:30) And Moses is the one who performed the signs before the people. Aaron brings the words, Moses brings the signs, and everybody has a job.
The answer is signs, bakers. “And Moses performed the signs before the people…” (Exodus 4:30) Aaron speaks, and Moses shows. That's a good division of labor.
The answer is that they believe, friends. The text says, “…and they believed.” (Exodus 4:31) They hear the words and see the signs. After all the warnings, this is a good moment.

The answer is affliction, friends. The people heard that “…the LORD had attended to the Israelites and had seen their affliction…” (Exodus 4:31) The news is that God has seen what they're going through. After that, “…they bowed down and worshiped.”
